back: Each input in the domain has exactly one output.
Domain: allowed inputs. Range: resulting outputs.
No zero denominators, no negative square roots, log arguments > 0.
Reflection of $y = f(x)$ in $y = x$; domain and range swap.

front: How can you tell from a graph whether it is a function?
back: Vertical line test: every vertical line meets the graph at most once.

front: What do $f(x) = x^2$ and $f: x \mapsto x^2$ mean, and what is $f(3)$?
back: Both define the same rule (input $x$, output $x^2$). $f(3) = 9$ is the output for input 3.
$2 \le x < 5$: square bracket includes the endpoint, round bracket excludes it.

front: Range of $f(x) = x^2 + 1$, $x \in \mathbb R$? And for $-1 \le x \le 2$?
back: $f(x) \ge 1$. On $[-1, 2]$: $1 \le f(x) \le 5$ (minimum at the vertex, maximum at the far endpoint).

One-to-one: each output comes from exactly one input (passes the horizontal line test). Many-to-one: some output has several inputs (e.g. $x^2$ on $\mathbb R$). Only one-to-one functions have inverses.
$x$, for every $x$ in the domain of $f$ — the inverse undoes $f$. Also $f(f^{-1}(x)) = x$ for $x$ in the domain of $f^{-1}$.
